# cipherstash_zerokms_keyset_grant (Resource)

Grant a ZeroKMS client access to one keyset. This resource manages a single client/keyset pair, not the client's full set of grants. Your application must still select the keyset in its SDK configuration.

Destroy revokes only this grant; it does not delete the client or keyset, or change other grants. Changing either ID replaces the grant without transferring any other grants.

Give each pair one owner. Do not manage it from another Terraform resource, state, or provisioning worker. Import an existing pair rather than creating it again. This includes the automatic default-keyset grant of a `cipherstash_zerokms_client`: the client resource manages identity only and does not require that grant to remain present.

Live Development API probes added and revoked an additional grant while the creation/default grant remained. Revoking the creation/default grant with another grant present returned HTTP 500, as did revoking a final grant to a nondefault keyset that was the client's creation keyset. Inventory confirmed those failed revocations left grants present. The cause is unresolved; do not rely on creation-grant removal in an automated lifecycle. Full Terraform keyset/grant lifecycle verification and live zero-grant inventory evidence remain outstanding. Inventory absence does not prove immediate credential invalidation. See the README's live verification limits.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `client_id` (String) ID of an existing ZeroKMS client, as a lowercase UUID. Changing this value replaces the grant; it does not copy the client's other grants.
- `keyset_id` (String) ID of an existing keyset, as a lowercase UUID. Changing this value replaces the grant. A disabled keyset can still have grants; a grant does not enable it.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Grant ID in the format `client UUID/keyset UUID`. Use the same format to import an existing grant.
